component.name: Apache Pulsar
component.description: Distributed pub-sub messaging and streaming platform. The security policy notes that Pulsar's security model is not formally or explicitly defined, but records two long-standing design assumptions: Pulsar Functions and connectors execute fully trusted code, and clusters rely on network-perimeter security.

externalReferences.comment: Source security model document; this file is a structured translation of it.
Authoritative security policy referenced by the SECURITY.md summary.

threats.name: Code execution through Pulsar Functions and connectors
threats.description: The function instance runtime exists to run user-provided code: remote code execution is its core purpose, not a flaw. The thread and process runtimes can read or modify any files and state accessible to the process they run in, and the Kubernetes runtime, on its own, does not restrict access to resources in the Kubernetes cluster (the project provides hooks for custom Kubernetes-runtime hardening, but such hardening is not part of the project). Reports that the function instance runtime allows running user-provided code and results in an RCE describe expected, by-design behaviour, not a security issue.

threats.name: Deliberate denial of service by a perimeter-trusted client
threats.description: Pulsar is designed to be deployed behind a trusted network perimeter where only trusted users can reach the cluster, and the project does not implement explicit controls against malicious denial-of-service attacks. Reports that a perimeter-trusted client can cause a denial of service generally fall outside Pulsar's threat model.

threats.name: Unintentional denial of service
threats.description: Overload caused by improper configuration or thundering-herd effects. Rate limiting exists to mitigate this class of unintentional denial of service, but it is not a defense against a deliberate denial of service by an attacker.

controls.name: Run only fully trusted code in Pulsar Functions and connectors
controls.description: Pulsar Functions and connectors must only run code that is fully trusted, since the available execution models let the code modify its environment and no runtime hardening is part of the project.

controls.name: Deploy behind a trusted network perimeter
controls.description: Deploy Pulsar behind a trusted network perimeter where only trusted users can reach the cluster; the project relies on network-perimeter security rather than implementing explicit anti-DoS controls.

controls.name: Rate limiting
controls.description: Rate limiting built into Pulsar mitigates unintentional denial of service, such as improper configuration or thundering-herd effects. It is not a defense against deliberate denial of service.

controls.name: Run a supported version
controls.description: Security fixes are made to supported versions (listed in the Pulsar release policy); users should upgrade to a supported version to receive security updates.
